correct_completion: the students rushed out of the classroom.
full_sentence: Lessons over, the students rushed out of the classroom.
acceptable_variants: the students hurried out of the classroom.
the students left the building quickly.

options.text: so the students rushed out of the classroom.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result clause. An absolute phrase is followed directly by the main clause, not by a linking word.

options.text: the students rushed out of the classroom.
because the students rushed out of the classroom.
options.why_wrong: 'Because' introduces a subordinate clause, so the sentence still lacks a main clause after the absolute phrase.

options.text: the students rushing out of the classroom.
options.why_wrong: This is a participle phrase with no finite verb, so it cannot function as the main clause of the sentence.

grammar_focus: Absolute (verbless) clauses followed by a main clause
explanation: An absolute phrase has its own subject but no finite verb, and it is followed by a main clause with a subject and verb. Learners often add a linking word such as 'so' or 'because' here, which breaks the structure of the absolute phrase.
translation: Com as aulas terminadas, os alunos saíram correndo da sala.
